subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The architectural approach is sound and minimal: resolve_source() transforms the optional 'source' field into the surface-appropriate inline field BEFORE validate_request, so the closed schema validator and all downstream code see a normal inline request. This is the correct and only placement: _require_exact_keys (schemas.py:78-80) rejects any key outside {surface, <expected>}, so 'source' MUST be removed before validate_request runs. The surface-discriminator map, extension-based format detection, and mutual-exclusion check all trace cleanly to AC1-AC8, C1-C4, DONT1-4. HOWEVER the shown implementation code has one hard contract violation (AC6 malformed-content) and one code/prose mismatch (D5 URL rejection). The AC6 violation: _load_json and _load_jsonl call json.loads without converting json.JSONDecodeError -> RequestValidationError. Per Python docs (https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html) json.JSONDecodeError is a subclass of ValueError and thus a SIBLING of RequestValidationError (schemas.py:12), not a child. control_plane.create catches ONLY RequestValidationError (control_plane.py:32) and mcp_boundary.handle (mcp_boundary.py:40-60) has no surrounding try/except, so malformed JSON/JSONL raises an UNCAUGHT exception instead of the typed INVALID_REQUEST AC6 requires. The design's own 'cleaner: catch RequestValidationError only' note makes this worse; only the dirty 'except (RequestValidationError, Exception)' variant would mask it, at the cost of hiding real bugs.

blockers.finding: Malformed .json or .jsonl content raises json.JSONDecodeError, which is NOT a RequestValidationError (both are sibling subclasses of ValueError per https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html and schemas.py:12). control_plane.create's 'except RequestValidationError' (control_plane.py:32) will not catch it, and mcp_boundary.handle (mcp_boundary.py:40-60) has no surrounding catch, so the exception propagates uncaught instead of returning a typed INVALID_REQUEST. AC6 explicitly requires 'malformed content ... return a typed INVALID_REQUEST diagnostic.' The design's own 'cleaner: catch RequestValidationError only' note makes this unavoidable; only the dirty broad-Exception variant would mask it (while hiding real bugs).
blockers.in_scope_remediation: Inside sources.py, wrap parsing and convert to RequestValidationError: (a) _load_json: try json.loads(path.read_text()) except json.JSONDecodeError as e: raise RequestValidationError(f'source JSON is malformed: {e}'); (b) _load_jsonl: same per-line; (c) wrap file reads (open/read_text) to convert OSError/PermissionError to RequestValidationError for robustness. Keep control_plane catching ONLY RequestValidationError (the design's 'cleaner' variant). Add malformed .json and .jsonl cases to test_sources.py for AC6/AC8 evidence.

validation.notes: Non-blocking CONCERNs: (1) D5 prose promises explicit URL-prefix rejection (http/https/ftp) but _load_items has no such check - URLs fail IMPLICITLY via Path().is_file()==False ('source file not found'). No fetch occurs (C1/DONT1 hold functionally), but C1 evidencePolicy=static_check, so a verifier pattern-matching for URL rejection will not find it. Recommend adding an explicit startswith check OR revising D5 prose. (2) Design shows 'except (RequestValidationError, Exception)' then 'actually cleaner: catch RequestValidationError only'; the broad variant masks the AC6 bug AND real bugs. Use the clean variant + fix AC6 inside sources.py. (3) Minor: empty-string or non-string 'source' - Path('')/Path(non-str) behaves oddly (TypeError uncaught on non-str). Add type/non-empty guard. (4) '~' paths: Path('~/x').is_file()==False -> 'file not found'; acceptable per threat model. CONFIRMED correct (no action): resolve_source->validate_request ordering for ALL surfaces incl queue; queue+options+source case passes _require_exact_keys cleanly; MCP boundary passes request dict containing source through unchanged; mutual-exclusion via 'if target_field in result' is correct; resolve_source returns dict copy (dict(request)) so original request is not mutated (DONT3/AC5 hold).

tradeoffs: Pre-validate_request resolution keeps the schema validator pure and closed (no 'source' awareness leaks into schemas.py), at the cost of resolve_source duplicating the surface->field mapping that schemas.py also encodes implicitly - two places must stay in sync if surfaces change.
Extension-based format detection is dead-simple and matches 'agent controls file content', but offers no content-sniffing fallback if an agent misnames a file.

Catching only RequestValidationError at the control plane (clean) requires sources.py to be exhaustive about converting every failure mode - any missed conversion (the current JSONDecodeError gap) becomes an uncaught crash rather than a typed diagnostic.

documents.proposal:
# Proposal: Add file-source batch loading

## Why

Gravy's create call currently requires all items passed inline in the MCP arguments. For large batches (200+ card verifications), this means a massive JSON payload in a single MCP tool call — awkward for agents to construct and wasteful to transmit. The agent typically already has the batch data in a file (CSV from a query, JSONL from a generator). Forcing it to inline-serialize 200 items into the create call is unnecessary friction.

## User Outcomes
- An agent can create a review from a file (CSV/JSON/JSONL) instead of inline items, with one MCP call regardless of batch size.
- The file is loaded server-side at create time; the reviewer sees the same review page they'd get from inline items.
- Existing inline-item creates are unchanged (backward compatible).

## What Changes
- Surface requests accept an optional `source` field (a local file path). When present, Gravy loads items from the file instead of the inline `items`/`criteria` array.
- Approved formats: CSV (one item per row, first column = item label), JSON (array of strings or objects with a `label`/`item` key), JSONL (one JSON object per line).
- `validate_request` resolves the source file before schema validation, producing the same parsed request shape downstream.
- File must be a local path readable by the Gravy process. No URL fetch.

## Scope

### In Scope
- `source` field resolution in `schemas.py` / `validate_request` — load items from file, then validate as usual.
- CSV, JSON, JSONL format support.
- Works for gallery, pairwise, checklist, queue (surfaces that take item lists). Form takes field descriptors, not items — `source` maps to field names from a CSV header or JSON keys.

### Out of Scope
- URL fetching (local files only — no SSRF surface).
- Pagination or progressive loading (the file is read once at create time; all items load into the review).
- Writing or updating source files (read-only).
- New surfaces.

### Must Not
- Fetch remote URLs or execute code in source files.
- Accept source files outside the local filesystem.
- Break existing inline-item creates.

## Constraints from Discussion
- `source` is an additional input option, not a new surface or pagination mechanism.
- Approved formats only (CSV, JSON, JSONL); reject unknown formats with a typed error.
- Backward compatible: `items`/`fields`/`criteria` still work when `source` is absent.

## Discovery Agenda
- Exact resolution point: should `source` be resolved in `validate_request` (schema layer) or in the control plane (before validate)? Schema layer is cleaner — the parsed request is identical downstream.
- Form surface: `source` maps to field names (CSV header row or JSON keys). Confirm this is useful vs confusing.
- Error handling: missing file, malformed CSV, empty file — all return typed `INVALID_REQUEST` diagnostics.

# Agreement: Add file-source batch loading

## Objectives
- Eliminate the inline-payload friction for large batches.
- Keep it as an input option — no surface/schema/UI changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 (Source loading):** When `source` is present in the request, Gravy loads items from the local file and the review is created with those items — identical to passing them inline.
- **AC2 (CSV format):** `.csv` files are parsed as first-column item strings (one item per row).
- **AC3 (JSON format):** `.json` files are parsed as an array of strings.
- **AC4 (JSONL format):** `.jsonl` files are parsed as one JSON string per line.
- **AC5 (Backward compatible):** Requests without `source` are unchanged — inline `items`/`criteria`/`fields` work exactly as before.
- **AC6 (Error handling):** Missing file, malformed content, empty item list, and unknown format all return a typed `INVALID_REQUEST` diagnostic.
- **AC7 (Surface mapping):** `source` populates `items` for gallery/pairwise/queue, `criteria` for checklist, `fields` for form — based on the surface discriminator.
- **AC8 (Tests):** Source resolution tests for each format + error cases + backward-compat assertions.

## Success Criteria
- An agent creates a review from a 200-item CSV file with one MCP call, and the reviewer sees all 200 items on the review page.

## Constraints
- Local files only (no URL fetch).
- Read-only (Gravy never writes to source files).
- Approved formats only (CSV, JSON, JSONL); reject unknown extensions.
- `source` and inline items are mutually exclusive — reject if both present.

## Avoidances
- Do not fetch remote URLs.
- Do not write to or modify source files.
- Do not change existing inline-item create behavior.
- Do not add new surfaces or pagination.

## Discovery Findings (carried into design)
- Resolution point: a `resolve_source(request)` function called in the control plane before `validate_request`. Returns a new dict with `source` removed and the surface-appropriate field (`items`/`criteria`/`fields`) populated. `validate_request` and everything downstream sees a normal inline request.
- Surface discriminator (`request["surface"]`) determines which field to populate: gallery/pairwise/queue → `items`, checklist → `criteria`, form → `fields`.
- Format parsing is dead simple: CSV first-column-per-row, JSON array of strings, JSONL one-string-per-line. No object extraction or header detection — the agent controls the file content.
- Errors raise `RequestValidationError` which maps to `INVALID_REQUEST` in the control plane.
documents.design:
# Design: Add file-source batch loading

## Architecture

New `sources.py` module with one function: `resolve_source(request)`. Called from the control plane before `validate_request`. Reads a local file (CSV/JSON/JSONL), produces a flat list of item strings, injects them into the request dict as the surface-appropriate field. Everything downstream sees a normal inline request.

No changes to surfaces, schemas, builders, or lifecycle. One new module + one control-plane call site + tests.

## LBP Decisions

### D1: `resolve_source()` lives in a new `sources.py` — not in schemas.py
Keeps file I/O out of the pure schema validator. `sources.py` imports `RequestValidationError` from `schemas.py` for typed errors. The control plane calls `resolve_source()` then `validate_request()` — two clean steps.

### D2: Surface discriminator determines the target field
`request["surface"]` tells `resolve_source` which field to populate:
- `gallery`/`pairwise`/`queue` → `items`
- `checklist` → `criteria`
- `form` → `fields`

The file always produces a flat list of strings. For form, those strings become field names (all type "text").

### D3: Format detection by file extension
- `.csv` → `csv.reader`, first column of each row
- `.json` → `json.load`, expect a JSON array of strings
- `.jsonl` → one `json.loads` per line, expect a string per line
- Other extensions → `RequestValidationError("source format must be .csv, .json, or .jsonl")`

### D4: `source` and inline items are mutually exclusive
If both `source` and the inline field (`items`/`criteria`/`fields`) are present, raise `RequestValidationError`. This prevents ambiguity.

### D5: Local paths only — explicit URL rejection
Reject any `source` value starting with `http://`, `https://`, or `ftp://` with a typed `RequestValidationError`. This makes the local-only constraint explicit (static-checkable), not just an implicit `is_file()` failure. Also guard: `source` must be a non-empty string (reject empty/non-string values with a typed error).

### D6: All errors convert to RequestValidationError (AC6)
`_load_json` catches `json.JSONDecodeError` → `RequestValidationError("source JSON is malformed")`. `_load_jsonl` catches per-line `json.JSONDecodeError` → same. File read errors (`OSError`) → `RequestValidationError("source file not readable")`. The control plane catches only `RequestValidationError` and returns `INVALID_REQUEST`. No uncaught exceptions escape the boundary.

## Implementation Strategy

### `src/gravy/sources.py` (new)
```python
"""File-source resolution for batch review loading."""
from __future__ import annotations
import csv
import json
from collections.abc import Mapping
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from .schemas import RequestValidationError

_SOURCE_FIELD = {
    "gallery": "items", "pairwise": "items", "queue": "items",
    "checklist": "criteria", "form": "fields",
}
_REMOTE_PREFIXES = ("http://", "https://", "ftp://")


def resolve_source(request: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """If request contains 'source', load items from the file. Otherwise pass through."""
    result = dict(request)
    source = result.pop("source", None)
    if source is None:
        return result

    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source.strip():
        raise RequestValidationError("source must be a non-empty file path")

    surface = result.get("surface", "")
    target_field = _SOURCE_FIELD.get(surface)
    if target_field is None:
        raise RequestValidationError(f"source is not supported for surface '{surface}'")

    if target_field in result:
        raise RequestValidationError(f"provide either 'source' or '{target_field}', not both")

    result[target_field] = _load_items(source)
    return result


def _load_items(source: str) -> list[str]:
    if source.startswith(_REMOTE_PREFIXES):
        raise RequestValidationError("source must be a local file path, not a URL")
    path = Path(source)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise RequestValidationError(f"source file not found: {source}")
    ext = path.suffix.lower()
    if ext == ".csv":
        return _load_csv(path)
    if ext == ".json":
        return _load_json(path)
    if ext == ".jsonl":
        return _load_jsonl(path)
    raise RequestValidationError(f"source format must be .csv, .json, or .jsonl (got {ext})")


def _load_csv(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    try:
        with open(path, newline="") as f:
            items = [row[0] for row in csv.reader(f) if row and row[0].strip()]
    except OSError as e:
        raise RequestValidationError(f"source file not readable: {e}") from e
    if not items:
        raise RequestValidationError("source CSV contains no items")
    return items


def _load_json(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text())
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        raise RequestValidationError(f"source JSON is malformed: {e}") from e
    except OSError as e:
        raise RequestValidationError(f"source file not readable: {e}") from e
    if not isinstance(data, list) or not all(isinstance(x, str) and x for x in data):
        raise RequestValidationError("source JSON must be an array of non-empty strings")
    return data


def _load_jsonl(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    try:
        text = path.read_text()
    except OSError as e:
        raise RequestValidationError(f"source file not readable: {e}") from e
    items: list[str] = []
    for line_num, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            item = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
            raise RequestValidationError(f"source JSONL line {line_num} is malformed: {e}") from e
        if not isinstance(item, str) or not item:
            raise RequestValidationError(f"source JSONL line {line_num} must be a non-empty string")
        items.append(item)
    if not items:
        raise RequestValidationError("source JSONL contains no items")
    return items
```

### `src/gravy/control_plane.py`
Add `resolve_source` import and call before `validate_request`:
```python
from .sources import resolve_source

def create(self, surface: str, request: Mapping[str, Any]) -> LifecycleResult:
    try:
        resolved = resolve_source(request)
        parsed = validate_request(resolved)
    except RequestValidationError:
        return LifecycleResult(diagnostic=DiagnosticCode.INVALID_REQUEST)
    if surface != parsed.surface:
        return LifecycleResult(diagnostic=DiagnosticCode.INVALID_REQUEST)
    return self.lifecycle.create(parsed)
```

documents.executiveSummary:
# Executive Summary: Add file-source batch loading

## Outcome
Agents can now create reviews from a local file (CSV/JSON/JSONL) instead of passing all items inline in the MCP call. For large batches (200+ card verifications), this eliminates the friction of serializing hundreds of items into a single create call. The agent generates a batch file using whatever domain logic it has, then points Gravy at the path.

## Value / why it matters
The inline-items pattern worked fine for small batches but created real friction at scale — a 200-item create call is a massive JSON payload that's awkward to construct and wasteful to transmit. The file-source option lets agents leverage existing batch-generation tooling (queries, CSV exports, JSONL generators) and hand Gravy the path. One MCP call regardless of batch size.

## What changed
- New `sources.py` module: `resolve_source(request)` loads items from a local file before schema validation. Supports CSV (first-column-per-row), JSON (array of strings), JSONL (one string per line). All errors convert to `RequestValidationError` → `INVALID_REQUEST`.
- Control plane calls `resolve_source` before `validate_request` — everything downstream sees a normal inline request. Backward compatible.
- URL rejection (local files only), type/non-empty guard, mutual exclusion (source + inline items can't coexist).

## Verification
- TDD red→green. 18 targeted tests pass (14 source resolution + 4 control plane). Engineer confirmed 109 full suite.
- Design validated by adv-researcher (CONFLICT→resolved: AC6 error conversion, URL rejection, type guard).
- All formats tested: CSV, JSON, JSONL, malformed content, missing file, unknown format, empty file, mutual exclusion, URL rejection, surface mapping.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Minimal risk: additive module, one call site, backward compatible.
- Future: support image URLs or object items in source files (second CSV column, JSON objects). Out of scope.
